made.how: a fresh session: no tools, no MCP servers, an empty directory, only the brief

verdicts.note: Per-profile isolation via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, the claude-<name> wrappers and the default profile taking bare `claude` are all documented. The package's origin (claude-code-nix) is never stated. The shared CLAUDE.md shows up only as the name `sharedMemory` and the read-only symlink comment.

The docs only say there is a macOS-only `app` option consumed by the freerdp bridge. Saved hosts and rdp-<name> commands appear only as names (hosts, hostCmd, hostAliasPrefix). Reading the password from the Keychain is not mentioned in this part.
Identity, the delta diff formatter and gh are all documented.
Keep-alives appear only as option names (serverAliveInterval, serverAliveCountMax). The single doc comment is about replicating the default config, not keep-alives.

The configurations table (hostname, system, nixType, username, version), local sub-flakes and nixos/home configurations are conveyed. darwinConfigurations appears only as a name. Justfiles and scripts for build, switch and inspect are only referenced in passing ('see justfile').

The sub-flake with the mkNixos/mkHome factories is documented. Nothing says the machines are bare metal. The system module set, the NixOS-only home modules and the one-node-per-host layout are not described (only genHost hints at the last).
Only boilerplate section headers. Nothing says it turns off GUI apps or pairs with core.headless.
Own tailnet node, Tailscale SSH (`tailscale up --ssh`) and trusting tailnet traffic are all documented.

Individual app modules exist (discord, minecraft, proton-pass, spotify, vscode, vivaldi). Steam is implied only by `remotePlay`. That these are installed by default and turned off on headless hosts is not stated.

The forced keyring for Chromium/Electron under Hyprland is documented, and 'both sessions' hints at a second session. The RX 7800 XT and ROCm are not stated (only lact/opencl names). Hyprland as the daily session with Plasma as fallback is not stated explicitly.
Waiting on a manually added hardware config is conveyed. Being a Plasma desktop on the defaults is not mentioned.
Headless, RX 7800 XT for GPU compute, OpenSSH, Tailscale node and the manual hardware config are all documented. ROCm is implied only by the `opencl` name.
Same as vgsquid-azul. Its being azul's twin is not stated, but the substance is identical.
The WSL2 sub-flake (custom nixos-wsl input) and the tailscale module are documented. The base environment module and the host are not described.
Own tailnet node on vghydra and the same Claude Code accounts as vgmacbook are both stated.

The sub-flake, Homebrew for GUI/App Store apps, the optional window manager (yabai), the status bar (SketchyBar), Homebrew aliases and the Tailscale CLI are documented. Hotkeys, keyboard layout and the host are not mentioned.
Dockable .app bundles wrapping shell commands, plus an RDP app for each host flagged app = true, are documented.

Homebrew casks and Mac App Store apps are well documented. FreeRDP to vghydra and the Claude profiles appear only as names (vghydra, profiles, defaultProfile). Tailscale is not mentioned, and neither is the personal/work split of the profiles.
It is evidently a stdenv build example. That it is deliberately not built and kept as a reference is implied only by the flake.nobuild.nix filename.
A Python flake under nix-templates with devShells. Its role as a template is implied by the path rather than stated.

unstated.claim: With force = false, a per-project direnv override of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR still wins over the default profile.
The bare package is installed only when no default-profile wrapper claims bin/claude; otherwise it is a profile collision (assertion).
Only files Claude Code never writes are symlinked; settings.json, .credentials.json, plugins and transcripts stay writable.
Sets a default editor.
Per-git-command pager overrides.
Git/GitHub shell aliases (e.g. gl, gs).
Reproduces the soon-deprecated default ssh config explicitly as match blocks.
homeConfigurations exist only for nix-eval debugging; home-manager is actually used as a NixOS module through the sub-flakes.
Exports reusable nixosModules/homeModules for sub-flakes via rootSelf.
Provides devShells and packages outputs.
commonPkgsConfig applies overlays and unfree settings to the extra nixpkgs channels.
pkgs-unstable and the flake inputs are passed to modules as specialArgs.
First join is interactive (`sudo tailscale up --ssh`); the host becomes reachable by its MagicDNS name.
Proton Pass is wrapped to force its password-store backend, because Electron otherwise falls back to obfuscated plaintext under Hyprland.
Vivaldi disables Qt wrapping to fix startup on Plasma 6 and has Widevine and proprietary codecs options.
Graphics stays on despite headless defaulting it off; Vulkan via mesa RADV.
Graphics stays on despite headless defaulting it off; Vulkan via mesa RADV.
The WSL tailnet node is separate from the Windows host's; first join is interactive with `--ssh`.
commonPkgsConfig and pkgs-unstable are passed through as specialArgs.
Homebrew cleanup is 'zap': anything undeclared is removed on rebuild, including cask preferences and support files.
Works around nix-darwin 25.11 emitting the old --cleanup flag by passing --force-cleanup itself.
autoUpdate/upgrade are off so rebuilds are idempotent; HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE is set.
HOMEBREW_BUNDLE_FILE points at the generated Brewfile, and lockfiles are disabled.
launchd agents run brew-update (metadata only) and brew-cleanup on a calendar schedule with an explicit PATH.
The module does not install Homebrew itself; activation skips with a warning until it is installed manually.
Policy: CLI tooling belongs in nix, not Homebrew.
The yabai module has an option for SIP-disabled full features.
Apps land in ~/Applications/Home Manager Apps via copyApps and are Spotlight-able.
A `terminal = true` option runs interactive commands inside the terminal emulator.
RDP apps read the password from the login Keychain (service rdp-<name>); with no entry they fall back to a terminal prompt; the password is visible on argv via /p:.
First run requires adopting already-installed casks with `brew install --cask --adopt`.
Mac App Store apps that are already installed are skipped and never touched by cleanup.
Uses a uv2nix workspace with editable overlays and sets UV_* environment variables in the dev shell.
